title: Six-month Nino 3.4 change asymmetry exceeded stationary IAAFT surrogate ranges in 1950-2025
abstract: We tested a prior negative six-month change statistic in a fixed NOAA ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 record for 1950-2025. We generated 999 iterative amplitude adjusted Fourier transform (IAAFT) surrogates. They retained the empirical distribution exactly and closely matched the power spectrum. The observed normalized cubic change statistic was -0.5066. No surrogate had a larger absolute value. The nominal two-sided tail fraction was 0.001, the test resolution. Month RMS scaling and endpoint trimming gave fractions of 0.001 and 0.004. Separate fits gave 0.207 for 1950-1987 and 0.006 for 1988-2025. These are follow-up tests of a pattern selected on the same data, not independent confirmation. Stationary surrogates do not retain seasonal dynamics. The results do not establish a physical feedback or reject all linear seasonal models. Approximate spectral constraints, nonstationarity, source reconstruction error and prior selection limit inference. The package gives code, exact source provenance, all scalar draws, a figure and an independent numerical audit. External monthly input stays outside the bundle.

display.caption: Red marks show observed six-month change asymmetry. Blue marks show central 95% surrogate ranges, not effect confidence intervals. Stationary surrogates retain the pooled distribution and approximate spectrum. The early era gave no clear departure.
